title: fix cookie name wrong if u use proxy server
body:
first off all, nice plugin! thx for your work.

i'm using this plugin with an proxy server, so the REMOTE_ADDR is the IP from the proxy, so the cookie name gets created with Proxy IP but checking the cookie works with comment author IP which is the users real IP.

With my changes, the Plugin first looks if HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR is set so if proxy is used you get the users real IP, if not set anything works as before.

title: bypass cookie-based user verification for authenticated cookie authors
body: This automatically bypasses the cookie check if the current user is the comment author (making the decision of "can_edit" controlled exclusively by the sce_can_edit filter), and adds a filter to allow someone to bypass the cookie check based on their own custom logic.

title: Added pre_comment_user_ip filter
body: At line 1095. This applies the filter (normally to anonymize the commenters IP address) when generating the hash to compare later. The hash is later compared with a newly generated one which uses the IP stored in the DB - which will have been (possibly) modified by the filter (as called by WP itself). If we don't do the filter when first generating the hash, then there will be a mismatch later and the user will not be given the edit possibility.

title: Fix the Webpack5 deprecation warning
body:
Hello,

this project uses the outdated [webpack-fix-style-only-entries](https://github.com/fqborges/webpack-fix-style-only-entries) plugin that is incompatible with `Webpack 5`.

Using `npm run build` appear the deprecation warnings:
```
webpack-fix-style-only-entries:
(node:18462) [DEP_WEBPACK_CHUNK_ENTRY_MODULE] DeprecationWarning: Chunk.entryModule: Use new ChunkGraph API
(node:18462) [DEP_WEBPACK_MODULE_INDEX] DeprecationWarning: Module.index: Use new ModuleGraph API
(node:18462) [DEP_WEBPACK_DEPRECATION_ARRAY_TO_SET] DeprecationWarning: chunk.files was changed from Array to Set (using Array method 'filter' is deprecated)
```

The author of the [webpack-fix-style-only-entries](https://github.com/fqborges/webpack-fix-style-only-entries) plugin recommends using the [webpack-remove-empty-scripts](https://github.com/webdiscus/webpack-remove-empty-scripts) plugin for Webpack 5.

This PR just replaces the outdated plugin with the actual version.

title: Restores comment edit UI for pending comments in block themes
body:
Resolves an issue where the comment editing interface was not visible for pending comments in block themes, such as Twenty Twenty-Four.

Block themes using the `core/comment-content` block sanitize and strip HTML from pending comments after standard content filters run. To address this, a new mechanism defers the injection of the Simple Comment Editing (SCE) interface.

*   Detects when the `core/comment-content` block is rendering for a pending comment.
*   Defers the SCE interface generation until *after* the block has rendered and its content has been processed.
*   Parses the rendered block content using the WordPress HTML API (with a regex fallback) to accurately re-insert the SCE UI alongside any moderation notes.
*   Bumps the plugin version to 3.4.1.

Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

title: GH#89: fix WooCommerce review rating editing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #89: keep SCE's enhanced rating picker inside existing-review editors and leave WooCommerce's native new-review control untouched.

- Merge current `master`, preserve both sets of FAQ/source changes, and rebuild conflicting generated assets from source.
- Listen for document-dispatched editor events, initialize one picker per editor, and synchronize stars/select values on save and cancel/reopen.
- Use the select value for submission; preserve ratings on text-only edits and handle ordinary comments, optional ratings, absent selections, and missing nonces safely.
- Reject malformed/out-of-range rating input without coercion. Retain nonce and ownership checks, return persisted metadata rather than request values, and refresh WooCommerce product rating aggregates after changes.
- Add regression coverage in `tests/WooCommerce_Test.php` using the existing real WordPress test framework; document editor behavior in `DESIGN.md`.

## Review and runtime testing

Tested in an isolated disposable database/site: PHP 8.4.25, WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.1, Storefront 4.6.2, Chromium desktop (1365×900) and mobile (390×844). Verified installed WooCommerce rating helpers, native star selectors, and `WC_Comments::clear_transients()` before changing integration behavior. No production deployment.

- **Passed:** native new-review form retains exactly one working star control and submits rating 4; existing-review editor also has exactly one picker.
- **Passed:** keyboard Enter selects a rating; saving updates text, rating metadata, and product averages. All integer ratings 1–5 persist correctly.
- **Passed:** cancel/reopen restores the saved stars AND select; save/reopen/reload preserves edited text and rating.
- **Passed:** text-only saves preserve existing ratings. Optional/unrated review editors permit text-only saves, remain unselected after cancellation, and can subsequently add a rating.
- **Passed:** ordinary comments submit/save/reopen without rating controls or JavaScript exceptions.
- **Passed:** negative, zero, >5, fractional, malformed, oversized, and array-valued ratings do not change saved ratings. Missing/invalid/array-valued WooCommerce nonces preserve rating metadata; responses report the actual saved rating. Invalid SCE nonces and unrelated anonymous visitors are denied, with content and rating unchanged.
- **Passed:** no page JavaScript errors in these paths; desktop/mobile screenshots inspected.

**Upstream limitation:** WooCommerce 11.2.1's native new-review template marks its hidden select `required` even when ratings are optional. The unrated fixture was submitted to WordPress with browser constraint validation bypassed solely to seed that test case. SCE's optional existing-review editor worked without this bypass. This PR deliberately does not change the native WooCommerce form.

## Automated verification

- `composer test` with cached current WordPress and a disposable database: **53 tests, 237 assertions**, single-site.
- `WP_MULTISITE=1 composer test` with the same isolated test setup: **53 tests, 237 assertions**, multisite.
- `composer lint`: PHPCS/PHPStan pass (existing PHPCS warnings).

- `npm run lint:js` and focused ESLint: pass (existing warnings).
- `php -l includes/WooCommerce.php`: pass.
- `npm run build`: pass (existing integrations-admin asset-size warnings).

Existing integration patterns: SCE document events and save-data filter; WooCommerce's native rating metadata and product-aggregate refresh. Regression tests follow `tests/Options_Test.php` and the existing `Plugin_State` fixture pattern. Runtime mutation/security checks above used real HTTP requests and real WordPress/WooCommerce metadata, not mocked permissions or input filters.

title: GH#123: preserve WP ULike controls after inline Save
body:
## Summary

Resolves #123.

WP ULike 5.2.4 deliberately excludes admin-AJAX requests from its frontend comment-button renderer. SCE's Save response therefore contains the edited text without the like button. Replacing the whole comment content removed the existing interactive control.

- Retain the original, comment-scoped automatic WP ULike control nodes when replacing saved text. Preserve live counts, liked state, handlers, and top/bottom/top-and-bottom placement.
- Match the edited comment's `data-ulike-type="comment"` and `data-ulike-id`, leaving post controls and other comments alone.
- If a response filter also generates like buttons, discard the returned copies rather than creating duplicates or replacing the live nodes.
- Do not change PHP endpoints, ownership/nonces, Save request counts, or WP ULike plugin files. With no existing automatic ULike controls, the ordinary replacement path is unchanged.
- Independent of PR #121: this branch starts from current master, not its motion-policy branch.

## Files and reference patterns

- `src/js/comment-editing/editing.js`: internal `updateCommentContent` helper used by the existing successful-Save path, before the existing `sceCommentSavePost` lifecycle event.
- `dist/sce-editing.js`: rebuilt using the configured webpack command. Unrelated admin-bundle regeneration drift was discarded.
- `README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `readme.txt`: integration contract and changelog.
- Reference: WP ULike's installed `wp_ulike_put_comments`, `WpUlikeInit::is_frontend`, and `wp_ulike_comments` markup contract; no external source files are modified.

## Local checks

Verified implementation: `cdcc59d`.

```sh
npx --no-install eslint src/js/comment-editing/editing.js
npm run lint:js
npm run build
git diff --check
```

All passed with no lint errors. Scoped ESLint reports seven existing warnings; the configured full JavaScript gate reports 113 existing warnings. Webpack has its existing admin-bundle size/performance warnings. No new test runner or test-only interface was introduced. PHP source and authorization endpoints are unchanged; local PHPUnit is not configured with a disposable `_test` database, and the browser site's database was not used for it. Current-head CI is required before merge.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: medium (third-party control lifecycle during successful Save).
- Level: runtime-verified.

Tested the actual built worktree on the configured local WordPress installation with Twenty Twenty-Five and WP ULike 5.2.4, using separate guest-owner, subscriber and non-owner Chromium sessions.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Guest submission and Save | Submitted and approved a real guest comment; Save persists, verified with WP-CLI. Its original ULike DOM node is retained. |
| Voted state | Like before Save remains liked with count +1 after Save; a subsequent click successfully unlikes it, reaching 0. |
| Repeated Saves | Original node identity and a single bottom control remain intact across repeated Saves. |
| Top and bottom | Real ULike setting renders two controls around the comment; Save preserves both original nodes and their order. |
| Top only | Real setting renders one leading control; repeated Saves preserve its identity and position. |
| Regenerated response copies | Temporary consumer of the existing `sce_return_comment_text` filter returned two real ULike controls. Captured Save-event response contains two copies, but rendered content contains only the original leading control. Consumer removed after verification. |
| No duplicate handlers | Repeated `SCE.init()` calls followed by Save keep one control; a vote after repeated Saves emits exactly one successful ULike request. |
| Subscriber | Own comment's Save persists; both live top/bottom controls survive, vote/unvote still works, and Cancel restores saved text without replacing them. |
| Unrelated controls | Post like control and the other comment's controls retain their identity. |
| Non-owner | No editor markup. Save with a valid guest per-comment nonce returns `success: false` / `You can no longer edit this comment.` Original text remains unchanged. |
| ULike inactive | Reload contains zero like controls; ordinary Save still persists, verified using WP-CLI. |
| Layout/diagnostics | Viewport screenshots inspected at 1280x900 and 390x844; controls retain placement and timer wraps on mobile without horizontal overflow. No browser console/page errors; successful Save and vote requests return HTTP 200. |

Temporary post/comments/user, vote data and the response-filter consumer are cleaned up. ULike settings and inactive status are restored. The local site remains available, linked to this fix's worktree. No release or live deployment is included.

Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.
